svg.title: Searchlight results to date
svg.desc: How the Searchlight test works, four findings with their evidence (pass rates with 95% ranges for search providers on two benchmarks and two coding agents, and how the agents searched), and the caveats for reading them.
svg.text: Does web search help coding agents do real work?
Results to date, 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-05 · 609 graded test runs · 2 AI coding agents · 6 search providers · 2 benchmarks
A research brief or a code fix
ends, or a question with a
was used. Briefs need the right
Every result below is a pass rate with its 95% range. Where two ranges overlap, the data cannot tell them apart.
Without search, both agents failed every
post-cutoff brief (0%). With any search setup,
Claude Code passed 62–95% and codex 72–94%, close
to the 95% and 89% reached when handed the answer
For work that depends on recent events,
search is not a tuning knob. It is the
difference between failing and passing, and
every provider tested closes most of the gap.
Pass rate on post-cutoff briefs (search gap bench)
The top provider was Parallel on Claude Code
(20/21) and Brave on codex (17/18), and most
intervals overlap. With 18–21 test runs per
provider, the bench cannot separate the leaders.
Choose on cost, latency and integration, then
measure on your own agent. Rankings did not
carry over from one agent to the other.
* Claude Code built-in search: the agent was not allowed to open pages, so it searched without reading them.
Not comparable to the provider rows; fixed for future runs.
memory does most of the work
In the bakeoff, answering from memory passed
within the margin of error, while tokens per
success rose from 20.9k (No search) to as much as
Search pays off where training data runs out.
Pass rate on documented-knowledge tasks (web search bakeoff, Claude Code)
Only 7% of searches about recent events read as
plain questions, and Codex leaned on site:
filters (31–67% of its provider queries). Agents
often skipped search and opened URLs they
remembered. Runs did better when the primary
The next gains are in how agents ask and what
primary sources first. These are correlations
· 18–42 test runs per provider: ranges are wide, and neighbouring positions are not rankings.
· Each provider ran through its own MCP server at a pinned version and default settings. Direct APIs, other search modes and other tools were not tested.
· Grading used automatic checks and blinded model graders. Provider dollar spend was only partly metered.
· Search behavior comes from 1629 logged queries; its links to pass rates are correlations.
